title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that compares ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to a single shared LLM candidate per intent. Generation used gpt-5-mini and the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator plus a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We (1) provide concise, auditable descriptions of the validator and repair operator; (2) report execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; deterministic repair invocations = 1); and (3) state operational limitations and interpretive consequences of a near-ceiling baseline. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, the single invoked repair trace, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle (see Disclosure Statement).

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) can reduce manual effort but raises an operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work shows that intent-to-configuration prototypes can fail in structured ways (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, grammar/constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Deterministic verifiers and emulator-backed validators are natural assurance layers, but fully instrumented, execution-grounded evaluations of conservative, low-hosted-call GVR designs remain scarce.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates a practical operational estimand: a shared-initial-generation design where a single LLM candidate per intent is (A) accepted as baseline and (B) passed to a deterministic validator and, if repairable, a deterministic repair operator (repair_budget ≤1). This shared-candidate estimand is relevant when hosted-model call budgets are constrained. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and appropriate exact-test justification for small-discordant-pair inference.
sections.related_work: LLMs for NetOps have been advanced along three related directions. Intent-to-configuration systems demonstrate synthesis capability but also expose structured-output failures; empirical prototypes and surveys report curated-condition success but note frequent failures without constraints (Nguyen et al., 2024) [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Mitigation approaches from adjacent domains—RAG, live schema grounding, and constrained decoding—show promise for reducing hallucinations in structured-output tasks (e.g., NL2SQL and document grounding). Formal verification methods (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) and emulator-based validators are viable assurance layers for reachability and isolation checks but are limited by dynamic control-plane phenomena and vendor idiosyncrasies (Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026) [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Generate–verify–repair architectures are proposed as pragmatic operational designs, yet public, preregistered, execution-grounded evaluations that isolate a low-hosted-call, repair-on-same-candidate estimand are limited; our study targets that gap (G2 in our evidence synthesis).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental plan: We preregistered a paired design (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration which was scored directly as the baseline arm and also fed to the guarded arm. The guarded arm invoked a deterministic validator and, when the validator reported a repairable violation, a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤ 1 deterministic repair attempt; no additional LLM calls). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator. The full preregistration, task manifest, prompts, provider traces, validator traces and repair traces are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256: e5c5fdbd717c...ff68; task-manifest SHA-256: eb2f045f8a62...fb4a).
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts (artifact-backed) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) computed on n = n10 + n01 = 1 yields p = 1.0 (artifact-backed). Complementary uncertainty quantification uses a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered primary-effect target (absolute 0.15) lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand.

Single repaired episode (archived exemplar): The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). The full per-episode scoring JSON and the deterministic repair trace for this episode are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/scoring and the repair-trace entry in the execution manifest); these artifacts contain the episode identifier, validator.violation_codes, the canonical repair rule applied (Insertion/Reordering/Preservation naming from the preregistered operator), and before/after normalized_configuration snippets. Readers may inspect the exact episode-level artifacts referenced by the manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) to reproduce the exemplar. (The confirmatory run invoked exactly one deterministic repair; the repair trace is included in the archived artifact bundle.)

Failure-accounting diagnostics: Syntactic/parse failures = 0; provider/API timeouts = 0. Provider-call accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. All per-episode validator traces and scoring JSONL artifacts are archived and form the basis for the primary counts (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv, artifact SHA-256 listed in analysis artifact manifest).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic validators provide structured, auditable violation codes that support low-churn, deterministic repairs; in a low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the shared-candidate guard preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate; practitioners seeking larger marginal improvements may prefer independent-resampling or LLM-invoked repair loops at greater provider cost and auditing burden.

Formal consequences of the realized baseline (power and inference limits): The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline ≈0.5 and targeted a 15-percentage-point absolute improvement at n = 200. The observed baseline (0.995) compresses possible discordant-pair counts and thus the realized ability to detect the preregistered effect under the paired estimand. Concretely, only n = 1 discordant pair was observed (n10 = 1, n01 = 0); with such a small number of discordants the exact McNemar p-value is uninformative for rejecting the null of no difference and the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] demonstrates that large preregistered effects (e.g., 0.15) are inconsistent with the observed data under this estimand. This is a post-hoc, artifact-backed limitation to confirmatory inference: the design remains valid for the estimand tested, but the realized near-ceiling baseline substantially reduces statistical sensitivity for large absolute-effect detection under the original power assumptions.
sections.conclusion: We ran an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and curated task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement; deterministic validators remain valuable, auditable assurance gates. All artifacts needed for reanalysis—including per-episode prompts/responses, provider traces, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, analysis scripts, paired contingency CSV, and bootstrap parameters—are archived in the study evidence bundle (see Disclosure Statement).

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256: e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: Generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle. The full per-task difficulty labels and counts for the 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator and validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.

Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; the observed single discordant pair (n=1) constrains confirmatory inference for large absolute-effect targets.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); the manifest provides an auditable distribution for readers who wish to inspect task difficulty stratification.
